- Our badge vendor sometimes records duplicates when attendees move between booths.
- We ran a sweep for fuzzy-match dedupe but can resend the normalized CSV if helpful.

Quick update on my sample (50 records):
- Exact email matches: 31
- Phone-only matches (email mismatch but same phone): 7
- No prior record in HubSpot: 12

Of the 31 exact matches, 9 were already in active deals (so we didn’t create new contacts). The phone-only crowd looks like badge scans where attendees used personal email addresses; our HubSpot rules prioritize email, so those scanned check-ins got merged to existing profiles under a personal email and weren’t counted as new event contacts.

Question for Karthik: do we have a way to temporarily relax email-priority matching for event imports so we can attribute contact credit to the GrowthWave campaign without creating duplicates? If not, we should prepare language for sponsors explaining matching heuristics.

Thanks for the sample, Ben. A couple quick points:
- Attribution policy: our ingestion pipeline applies the following priority — 1) UTM campaign match, 2) explicit form-source tag, 3) email + domain heuristics. Phone-only matches don’t create new canonical contacts by default to avoid duplicates.
- Temporary relaxation: we can run a one-off import that creates "event-only" contacts with a GrowthWave source tag and a de-duplication flag. That would preserve canonical customer records but still allow sponsor reporting to show event-level credit. It will require a brief ETL job and QA (1 business day).

I recommend we:
1) Create the event-only import (KA: infra + ops) and label all imported rows with growthwave_roadshow_2026.
2) Produce a reconciliation pivot that compares: raw check-ins vs hubspot canonical contacts vs event-only import.
3) Draft sponsor messaging that explains how we reconcile and what counts as "credited" contact vs "canonical" contact.

If you all agree I'll queue the ETL for Friday morning and we can have a reconciled report by end of day Friday.

Karthik
Director, Field Sales Ops
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai

Hi Elena — thanks for the patience and for the detailed files. Quick summary of where we landed after internal checks:

Key findings:
- Raw check-ins (GrowthWave tablets): 237 unique check-ins, of which 68 were flagged by GrowthWave as qualifying MQLs.
- HubSpot canonical contacts attributed to the event (initial export): 165 contacts. Many of the missing check-ins are phone-only or used personal emails and matched to existing canonical records, which suppressed "new contact" creation.
- Event-only import (growthwave_roadshow_2026): we created 220 event-only rows (we filtered obvious vendor duplicates and merged obviously repeated badge scans).
- Credited contacts for sponsor reporting: 185 unique contacts (this is the reconciliation view where we credit a contact if it appears in event-only import OR is an existing canonical with an interaction timestamp within 7 days of the event).

Outstanding items:
- 12 records remain ambiguous (fuzzy phone matches where two different emails share the same number). We recommend GrowthWave confirm email preference for those attendees if sponsor-level crediting is required.
- We should add a brief paragraph to the sponsor report that explains our matching heuristics and the difference between "credited for sponsors" vs "canonical contacts" in HubSpot.

Next steps (owners & timeline):
- Chloe: finalize sponsor-facing reconciliation csv and a short one-pager explaining heuristics (due Mon 8/31).
- Karthik: keep event-only import flagged and add an internal tag so marketing can filter those rows from nurture flows (done).
- Ben: share a short note for AE/CS teams on how to surface event-attributed contacts in outbound outreach (due Mon 8/31).

If this approach works for GrowthWave, we’ll send the reconciled CSV and the short explainer tomorrow and offer a 20-min walkthrough if the sponsor team wants more color.

Best,
Chloe Martin
Sr. Field Marketing Partner, Redwood Inference
